translations.text: And after Israel’s captivity and the destruction of Jerusalem, Jeremiah sat weeping and lamenting these laments over Jerusalem, and said:
How the city once full of people has sat apart, alone, and become like a widow, filled with sorrow! The ruler of the world among the nations has become subject to tribute.
She wept bitterly in the night, with her tears upon her cheeks. On that day she found no comforter among those who loved her. All her friends despised her and became like enemies to her.
Judah was led into captivity amid much suffering, in the distress of slavery and servitude. She dwelt among the nations and found no rest. All her pursuers overtook her among her enemies.

The roads of Zion mourned, because no one traveled to her annual festivals. All her gates were laid waste, and her priests [?], sigh, and groan. Her virgins were led into captivity, and she herself was embittered in her soul.
Her oppressors became her rulers, and her enemies rejoiced, because the Lord brought her low for her great wickedness. Her children were led into captivity before her oppressors.

All their splendor was taken away from the daughters of Zion. Their princes became like rams that could find no pasture. They gave their precious, precious possessions for food to revive themselves. They went on without their senses before their oppressors, driven by their pursuers.

Jerusalem remembered the days of her suffering and the days of her separation. She grieved over all the precious possessions she had acquired from the beginning. When her people fell into the hands of enemies, there was no one to help her. Those who hated her saw her, stamped their feet, and laughed at her captivity.
Jerusalem sinned grievously. Therefore all who praised her brought her low, because they saw her disgrace. She herself turned back and groaned.

Her uncleanness was before her feet, and she did not remember her latter end. She shed great tears, and there was no one to comfort her. See my suffering, Lord, for my enemies have risen up against me.
The oppressor stretched out his hand over my precious possessions. I saw the nations enter your sanctuary, though you had commanded them not to enter the place of your people.
All the people groaned as they searched for bread. They gave all their precious possessions in exchange for bread, to restore their lives. See, Lord, and look, for I have been despised.

I say to you, I say to you, travelers on the roads: turn, look, and see whether there has ever been pain like the pain that has come upon me. The Lord spoke against me and brought me low on the day of his anger and wrath.
From his heights he sent fire into my bones. He spread a net for my feet and turned me back. He brought me to ruin, leaving me all day long in suffering and sorrow.

The Lord rose early against my wickedness and laid his hand upon [?]. He made his yoke heavy upon my neck. My strength failed. The Lord delivered me into the hands of my pains, and I cannot find rest.
He wiped out the very best of my forces from my midst. He appointed a time of destruction against my chosen men. The Lord trod the winepress for the virgin daughter of Judah.

Because of this, behold, I have given myself to weeping. My eye has shed tears, because my comforters, who would restore my soul, have gone far from me. My children were delivered to destruction, because the enemy grew strong.
Zion stretched out her arms to God, and there was no one to comfort her. Her oppressors were all around her. Jerusalem became like an unclean woman among them.
The Lord God is righteous, for I provoked him to anger. Hear this, all you peoples, and see my pain. My maidens and my young men were led into captivity.
I called to those who loved me, and they scorned me. My priests and my elders perished here in this city. They searched for food to restore their lives, but none was found.
See, Lord, for I am distressed. My bones are troubled, my heart is wrung within me, and I have become embittered. Outside, the sword has bereaved me, as has death within.

Listen, listen to this: I groan and sigh, and there is no one to comfort me. All my enemies heard of my troubles and kicked me, because you made that day and called for that time. And woe, woe came upon me!
All the evils came before you. Strip them bare, just as you stripped me bare because of all my sins, for my groans have become many, and my heart is filled with sorrow.
How the daughter of Zion has been darkened by the fury of the Lord’s anger! He cast the glory of Israel from heaven to earth and did not remember his footstool on the day of his furious anger.

The Lord swallowed up every village of Jacob without pity. He tore down the strongholds of the daughter of Judah and did not spare them. He brought them down to the ground and dishonored their rulers and kings.
On the day of his furious anger, the Lord shattered all the horns of Israel and drew back his right hand before his enemies. Fire enveloped Jacob; it consumed and wore away everything around him.
He entered his own bosom [?] like an enemy, set his right hand against her, and killed all the beloved ones of the daughter of Zion. He poured out the fury of his anger upon her with fire.
The Lord became like an enemy and destroyed Israel. He destroyed its kings and all its strongholds, and he piled suffering upon suffering on the daughter of Judah.

He tore apart her tents as though they were a vineyard and ruined her annual festival. The Lord forgot the annual festivals and Sabbaths that Zion observed, and in the roar of his anger he enraged the kings, rulers, and priests.

The Lord rejected his altar and cast away his holy places. He demolished the towered walls of her temples. They raised their voices and shouted in the Lord’s house as on the days of her annual festivals.
The wall of the daughter of Zion fell in ruins. They stretched out a measuring line and did not draw back their hands. The monuments and walls mourned; all together they trembled and collapsed.
They demolished her gates to the ground and shattered her bars. Their kings and rulers were among the Gentiles. There were no laws or prophets, nor were there any who saw visions from the Lord.

The elders of the daughter of Zion came down, lay flat on the ground, and fell silent. They put dust on their heads and dressed in sackcloth. They cast the leaders of Jerusalem’s virgins down to the ground.

My eyes failed from tears, my belly was troubled, and my glory melted onto the ground because of the crushing of the daughter of my people, as children and nursing infants died throughout all the streets of the city.
They begged their mothers for bread and wine. As they wasted away, poured out their lives, and breathed their last, they lay fallen and scattered in the midst of the city.
What testimony can I give you, or to what can I compare you, daughter of Jerusalem? Who will comfort you, virgin daughter of Zion? For the cup of your ruin has become heavy. Who, then, can heal you?

Your prophets saw empty, groundless, and useless visions for you. They did not reveal your wrongdoing to you so that you might return from your captivity, but told you meaningless riddles and of expulsion from one’s own place.
All who passed along the road clapped their hands. They hissed and shook their heads at the daughter of Zion. “Is this the city,” they said, “the crown of glory, the joy of the whole earth?”

All your enemies opened their mouths against you. They hissed and ground their teeth and said, “Come, let us swallow her up! This is the day we were waiting for. Look, we have seen it, found it, and reached it!”
The Lord did what he said. He fulfilled the words he decreed in days long ago. He tore down and did not spare. He made your enemies rejoice over you and raised the horn of those who oppress you.
Let their hearts cry out to the walls of the daughter of Zion, and let them pour out tears like a torrent by day and night. Do not be silent, do not stop, and give your eye no rest from tears.

Rise to give thanks in the night, at the beginning of your watches. Pour out your heart like water before the Lord. Lift up your hands for the lives of the children who were wasting away from hunger at the head of the roads where you go out and come in.

Look, Lord, and see: to whom have you done this? [?] Will women eat the fruit of their own wombs? You have done [?]; you have cast the [?] inside, to slaughter within the Lord’s sanctuary the nursing children, the priest, and the prophet.

Old people and children alike lay asleep at the openings of the roads. Virgins and young men were led into captivity. You put them to the sword and killed them on the day of your anger. You slaughtered and crushed them and did not spare them.

You summoned around me, as on the day of the yearly festivals of my exile. On the day of the Lord’s indignation and anger, no one was found surviving or remaining, to be kept safe as all my enemies multiplied.
Mighty God, look upon my misery. He took hold of me with the rod of his indignation.
And he brought darkness upon me, and not light.
Nevertheless, he continually turned his hand against me.
He wore away my skin and my flesh; he shattered all my bones.
He built against me and enclosed my head.
And he labored and made me sit in darkness, like one long dead.
He heaped things upon me, and I can no longer move. He made the weight upon me heavier than bronze.
For even though I said, “I will call out and cry aloud,” my prayer is shut out and barred from his presence.
He put a barrier across my roads and gravel to make my paths frightening.
He became to me like a bear lying in wait and like a lion in hiding.
He came after me, pursued me, caught up with me, and abandoned me, and brought me to ruin.
He entered his own bosom and filled me with arrows as though I were a target.
He split my kidneys in two and filled me with arrows,
and made me a laughingstock to my people and their song all day long.
He fed me gall and made me drink bitterness.
He filled my teeth with stones and fed me ashes.
He cast my soul away from peace; I forgot good things.
My victory and my hope from the Lord have perished.
I remembered my misery and my persecutions.
Bitterness and anger came to my remembrance together; my soul grew weary within me.
I laid this in my heart; therefore I will endure.
The Lord’s mercies are inexhaustible, and his compassion does not diminish.
With the renewal of the morning, your faithfulness increases.
My soul spoke a word: “The Lord is my portion; therefore I will wait for him.”
God is kind to those who wait for him, for the soul that seeks him.
It is good to wait for him faithfully and to rest in the salvation of the Lord.
It is good for a person to take up the yoke of humility from his youth.
Let him sit alone and silent in his house, for he himself took your yoke upon himself.
Let him put his mouth to the dust, because there is hope.
Let him offer his cheeks to those who strike him; let him be filled with insults.
But the Lord will not reject forever.
The one who caused suffering will also show mercy according to his abundant mercy.
He did not give an answer from his heart, and he humbled the children of men.
To bring low beneath his feet all the prisoners of the earth, to hand a man over at the Lord’s judgment,
to reject a man’s rights before the face of the Most High.
The Lord does not see the punishment of a person in judgment.
He did not say, “Thus says the Lord,” and it happened; he did not command it.
From the mouth of the Most High neither evil nor good will come forth from here.
Why should a living person complain, or a man about his sins?
Our ways were examined and rebuked; let us return to the Lord.
Let us lift up our hearts with our hands, together with our hands, to the heights of heaven.
We sinned and acted wickedly, and you were not pleased with us.
You came to visit in indignation and anger, and you pursued us; you slaughtered us and did not spare us.
You closed off the heavens with clouds so that our prayers would not reach you.
You cast us out and rejected us as despised, and you made us dishonored among the armies of the nations.
You opened all the mouths of our enemies against us.
Dread and fear came upon us, ruin and destruction.
My eyes poured down streams of water over the ruin of the daughter of my people.
My eyes have received, and I will not be silent, and I will not hear.
until the Lord appears and sees from heaven.
My eye will shed tears over my soul more than all the daughters of my cities.
They hunted me like bird hunters; my enemies hunted me without cause.
They stifled my life in a pit and placed a rock over me.
The waters overflowed above my head, and I said, “I say, look, I have been rejected.”
I called on your name, Lord, from the pit of affliction.
And you heard my voice. Do not hide your ear from my pleas, but give me relief and save me.
You drew near to help me and said [?], “On the day you call to me, do not be afraid.”
You pleaded my cause, Lord; you redeemed my life.
You saw the violence done to me, Lord; you judged my case.
Did you see all my rightful claims? You looked upon all my plans.
You heard, Lord, the insults and all their schemes against me.
At the lips of those who rise against me all day long.
I took note of their sitting down and their rising up, from their schemes.
Look upon the pride in their eyes, and repay them, Lord, bringing their recompense upon their own heads.
Repay them according to the hardness of their hearts.
May you pursue them in your wrath and destroy them in your anger beneath the heavens.
How the gold has grown dull! The white silver has changed color. Their precious stones melted and were scattered at the entrances to their roads.
The precious sons of Zion, worth more than precious stones—how they were regarded as earthenware vessels, made by the hands of potters!

Like dragons, they bared their breasts and nursed their young. The daughters of my people were tormented by blows, for there is no healing for them, and they suffered like ostriches in the wilderness.
The tongues of nursing infants stuck to the roofs of their mouths because of their thirst. Children asked for bread, and there was no one to break it for them.
Those who ate food perished along the roads. Those who had been nurtured and cherished in laps were cast into the lap of refuse and rolled about, smeared with filth.
The lawlessness of the daughter of my people became greater than the lawlessness of Sodom, which was overthrown. They rose up in haste and hurry, and nowhere was there any labor of their hands.
Their Nazirites were purified like snow and became white like milk; they were refined like sapphire stones in their recompense.
Their appearance became darker than coal, and no one recognized them as they lay along the roads. Their skin clung to their bones; they grew hard and became like dried wood.
The wounded among the bodies of those who had fallen by the sword looked better than those who had fallen from hunger. The wounded went away, group after group of men.
The hands of compassionate women cooked their own children, and they became food for them at the destruction of the daughter of my people.
The Lord brought and fully unleashed his furious anger. He poured out his furious anger and kindled a fire in Zion, and it consumed her foundations.
The kings of all the earth, who dwelt throughout the world, did not believe that an enemy would enter through the gates of Jerusalem.
Because of the sins of their prophets and the sins of their priests, who shed the blood of the righteous in their midst.
Their forces were shaken and staggered at the exits of the roads. They were defiled and stained with the blood of the dead, so that they could not take their clothes off without defilement.
“Keep away!” Call them unclean. “Keep away! Keep away! Do not come near!” For they were shaken and inflamed. Say among the nations, “Let them no longer continue to dwell among them.”
While we were alive, our eyes grew weak looking for help, for we had vainly set them to watch for worthless things.

The face of the Lord has turned away from them and will no longer look upon them. They showed no respect for the priests, had no mercy on the elders or on their children. We kept watch, looking toward nations that could not save us.
They hunted us; a little more, and they would have utterly destroyed and wiped us out of our cities. The hour has come, the time has arrived; our days are ended, our times are fulfilled.
Our pursuers moved swiftly over the mountains like the eagles of heaven. They soared over the high mountains, and in the wilderness they lay in ambush and surrounded us.
They encircled Christ the Lord, the breath of our faces, in their destruction, while we thought that under his shelter we would dwell and live among the nations.
Rejoice and be glad, daughter of the Edomites, who dwell in the land of Uz. This cup will come upon you; you will rise and drink, become drunk, and vomit.
Your lawless deeds have come to an end, Zion, and he will no longer discipline you. He has called your lawlessness to account, daughter of Edom; he has revealed all your ungodliness.
The Prayer of Jeremiah the Prophet
Remember, Lord, what has happened to us. Look and see our disgrace.
Our inheritance has passed to foreigners, and our dwelling has become a place of exile.
We were left orphans, and we had no father; our mothers were like widows in our time.
We drank our water for a price, and our wood was without payment.
It came upon our necks; we were driven away and found no rest.
The Egyptians and the Assyrians extended their hands to satisfy us with bread.
Our fathers sinned and are no longer anywhere among us, and those sins of our fathers have come upon us.
Slaves ruled over us, and there was no one among us to rescue us from their hands.
Come, let us bring provisions inside, away from the sword of the wilderness.
Our skin became stiff like an old oven because of the fury of hunger.
They dishonored the women in Zion and the virgins in the cities of Judah.
They hung the elders by their thumbs and did not spare the old women.
The finest of our men raised their voices and wailed, and the young men grew weak from being struck with wood.
The elders withdrew from the gates, and the chosen men fell silent in their praises.
Our hearts abandoned joy, and the praises of our dances turned into mourning.
The crown has fallen from our heads. Woe to us, woe to us, for we have sinned!
Because of this, we were given aching hearts; because of this, our eyes also grew dark,
because of Mount Zion, which has become a ruin, and foxes went in and out of its halls.
But you, Lord, remain forever, and your throne endures from generation to generation.
Why have you utterly forgotten us, struck us and abandoned us? Will you forsake us for so long?
Turn us back, Lord, and we will return. Renew us, Lord, as in the former days.
For you have utterly rejected us; the fury of your anger has raged against us to the utmost.
